learningObjective: Explain what continuous (iteration-level) batching is and why it improves throughput over static batching for LLM serving.

canonicalClaims.claim: Continuous batching rebuilds the batch at each model-forward iteration; new requests can join and finished ones leave without waiting for the whole batch to complete, keeping the GPU utilized under variable-length workloads.
conditions: Requests share the same model and can share a batched forward.
nonImplications: Does not imply per-request semantics change.
Does not require uniform progress across requests.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous batching requires all requests in the batch to make the same number of steps.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The exact point is that requests can join/leave freely per iteration.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous batching relies on per-request CUDA streams.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The mechanism is batching granularity, not stream parallelism.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous batching predicts multiple tokens per step for each request non-autoregressively.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Each iteration is still one autoregressive step per request; batching happens across requests.

implementationFacts: vLLM's scheduler runs continuous batching over PagedAttention KV cache.
Prefill can be interleaved with decode via chunked prefill + continuous batching (SGLang/vLLM).
performanceScenarios: The larger the variance in output lengths, the bigger the benefit vs static batching.
